note: This is an AI-generated sample project for testing.
title: The Last Light of Greyhaven
description: Explore a fading harbor, uncover the lighthouse keeper's secret, and restore the beacon before another ship is lost.

text: Welcome to Greyhaven, {player.name}.
You stand in the old harbor square, where fishing boats once crowded the water.
Tonight, the sea is unusually dark. The lighthouse has been unlit for three nights, and ships are beginning to avoid the coast.
The harbor master has left a note on the notice board: 'The beacon can be restored, but the keeper sealed the tower before he disappeared.'
You decide to find a way into the lighthouse and discover what happened.
A stone walkway leads north from the harbor square.
The tide has stained the lower stones, and small shells have collected in the cracks.
A set of fresh footprints crosses the damp path before disappearing near the shipyard.
Someone has been moving around the harbor recently.
You reach the old shipwright's yard.
Half-built boats rest beneath canvas covers, their wooden frames grey with age.
A workbench is scattered with nails, rope, and sketches of ships.
One drawing shows a lighthouse lens surrounded by two curved pieces of glass.
The ropewalk stretches east along the water.
Long coils of rope hang from wooden posts, stiff from years of salt and wind.
A ledger on a small table lists deliveries to the lighthouse keeper.
The last entry reads: 'One brass key returned for safekeeping.'
You enter a small cottage that once belonged to the harbor's lamp tender.
The room is tidy, despite the dust. A lantern sits beside a stack of maintenance records.
A note tucked inside the ledger says: 'The eastern door of the lighthouse is still secured. Keep the brass key away from the tide.'
Beneath the ledger, you find a small brass key.
This narrow storehouse smells of salt and old timber.
Empty crates are stacked against the walls.
A shipping label identifies several supplies as parts for the lighthouse's turning mechanism.
A second label is marked: 'Deliver only when the keeper is present.'
You walk along the eastern breakwater.
Waves strike the rocks below, sending spray over the low stone wall.
At the end of the path stands a heavy service door set into the lighthouse foundation.
A brass keyhole is visible beneath a faded emblem.

success.message: The brass key turns with a reluctant click. The service door opens, and a narrow passage leads into the lighthouse.

failure.message: The service door will not move. Its lock has a brass keyhole.

text: You follow a sloping path south of the square.
The path descends toward the low-tide shoreline.
An old bell hangs from a timber frame. Its rope has snapped, and the bell is silent.
A plaque reads: 'When the beacon shines, ring the bell to welcome the returning ships.'
The path ends at a stretch of dark shingle beach.
Pieces of driftwood lie scattered among the stones.
A half-buried crate bears the lighthouse's old crest, but its lid has been washed away.
The tide has left a trail of broken glass leading east.
You discover the remains of a small wreck beside the seawall.
Most of the vessel has been reduced to splintered wood.
A thick piece of blue glass is lodged between two beams. It resembles a lens from an old signal lamp.
You carefully take the blue lens. It may help you see through the dark passages below the cliffs.
A narrow stone stair climbs to the top of the seawall.
Below you, a dark opening appears between the rocks. The entrance is partly concealed by the tide.
A faint mark beside it resembles the shape of a glass lens.
The opening may lead beneath the cliffs.

success.message: The blue lens catches a trace of light and reveals the safe route through the opening. You descend into the sea caves.

failure.message: The passage is too dark to navigate safely. A blue signal lens may reveal the way.

text: An old boat shed stands between the square and the beach.
A single rowboat rests upside down on wooden supports.
Inside the shed, a charcoal sketch shows a tunnel beneath the lighthouse cliffs.
The sketch is labelled: 'Keeper's route — use only at low tide.'
You find a disused customs office.
A cracked window looks out over the harbor entrance.
Ledgers record the names of ships that once visited Greyhaven.
The final page lists three vessels that never returned after the lighthouse went dark.
This small square once served as the harbor's meeting place.
A dry fountain stands beneath a weathered statue of a sailor.
An inscription reads: 'A light is a promise made to those still at sea.'
The words seem more important now than they did when they were carved.
You discover a ruined lookout chapel on the western side of the harbor.
Its roof has fallen in, but a stained-glass window remains intact.
The glass depicts a lighthouse shining over a crescent moon.
A line beneath the window reads: 'The moon guides the keeper when the sun has gone.'
A narrow path winds behind the ruined chapel.
From here, you can see the entire harbor and the dark shape of the lighthouse.
A stone marker bears the names of the keepers who maintained the beacon.
The most recent name has been scratched away.
You step into a cavern beneath the cliffs.
The entrance behind you is narrow, and waves echo through the stone.
A pale line of mineral deposits marks the usual high-water level.
The blue lens helped you find a safe route down. You should keep an eye on the tide.

success.message: You climb back up the passage and emerge beside the harbor seawall.

text: A low arch leads deeper beneath the cliffs.
You must duck beneath the stone ceiling.
The floor is covered in smooth pebbles, polished by countless tides.
Scratches on the wall show that someone has used this passage many times.
The passage opens into an echoing chamber.
Every movement returns as a soft whisper from the walls.
A rusted lantern hangs from a hook, though there is no oil left inside.
A message scratched into the stone reads: 'Follow the sound of dripping water.'
You follow the sound into a chamber filled with slow-dripping water.
Small pools reflect the faint light from the entrance.
A narrow ledge runs along the eastern wall.
Beyond it, a dry shelf holds a bundle wrapped in oilcloth.
You unwrap the bundle on the dry shelf.
Inside is a chart showing the changing tides around Greyhaven.
The chart includes a note in the keeper's handwriting: 'The beacon's gears must be set at the turning of the tide.'
You take the tide chart. It may be essential to restoring the lighthouse.
A small alcove lies beyond the chart shelf.
The ceiling is covered in pale shells, and the walls glitter with tiny crystals.
A carved symbol shows the same two curved glass pieces seen in the shipwright's drawing.
The keeper must have used these caves to store notes about the beacon.
You reach a dry ledge overlooking an underground pool.
The water is perfectly still, despite the waves crashing outside.
An old iron ring is set into the stone, perhaps once used to secure a boat.
A final inscription reads: 'The sea remembers every light that has guided it home.'
The service passage opens into the lighthouse entrance hall.
Dust covers the floor, but a narrow trail suggests someone has walked here recently.
A spiral staircase rises through the center of the tower.
A door to the west leads back to the harbor.

success.message: You leave the lighthouse and return to the eastern breakwater.

text: You climb the first section of the spiral staircase.
The walls are lined with old photographs of lighthouse keepers.
The final photograph shows the missing keeper standing beside a covered lantern mechanism.
Someone has written beneath it: 'The light is not broken. It is waiting.'
You reach the upper lantern platform.
A great circular mechanism fills the center of the room.
Three empty fittings are set into its control panel: two curved slots and a narrow chart holder.
The mechanism appears to require the moon prism, the sun prism, and the tide chart.
A stairway continues upward toward the beacon chamber.

success.message: You fit the two prisms into their slots and place the tide chart in its holder. The mechanism begins to turn, and the upper doors unlock.

failure.message: The beacon mechanism remains still. It needs the moon prism, the sun prism, and the tide chart.

text: A western corridor branches away from the staircase.
Shelves contain logbooks from former lighthouse keepers.
Most entries describe ordinary maintenance, but the final pages mention a strange failure in the beacon's turning gears.
The keeper wrote that the two prisms had been separated for safekeeping.
You enter a small chart room.
A large map of the coastline covers one wall.
A crescent-shaped glass prism rests in a padded wooden case.
A label identifies it as the moon prism, one of the pieces needed by the beacon.
A narrow staircase leads to the keeper's archive.
Boxes of correspondence are stacked beneath a slanted window.
One letter explains that the moon prism was entrusted to the archivist after a storm damaged the tower.
The letter ends: 'Keep it apart from the sun until the tide is known.'
This chamber contains the remains of an old clockwork regulator.
Its gears are motionless, and a pendulum rests against the wall.
A diagram shows how the lighthouse mechanism follows the rise and fall of the tide.
The tide chart from the caves must contain the missing timing information.
An eastern corridor leads away from the main staircase.
The wall is lined with brass pipes and small inspection windows.
A steady draft rises from below, carrying the smell of oil and salt.
The keeper used this passage to reach the machinery without climbing the outer stairs.
You enter the lens workshop.
A worktable is covered in glass-cutting tools and polishing cloths.
A sun-shaped prism rests inside a padded metal frame.
This must be the sun prism described in the keeper's notes.
The workshop opens into a maintenance bay.
A large gear is mounted against the wall, its teeth worn smooth.
An oil-stained note says: 'Never force the turning gear. Align the prisms first.'
The warning explains why the beacon could not simply be restarted.
You find a narrow gear chamber beneath the eastern corridor.
Small wheels and levers connect to the mechanism above.
A brass plate bears three markings: moon, sun, and tide.
The same three symbols appear on the tide chart.
You enter the keeper's old living quarters.
A narrow bed, a desk, and a cold stove remain in the room.
The desk holds a half-written letter addressed to the harbor master.
The keeper wrote: 'I have hidden the prisms and chart until someone understands that the light must serve the ships, not the tower.'
A short stair descends into the lighthouse cellar.
Spare lantern glass and empty oil tins are stacked along the walls.
A small window looks out toward the sea caves.
The cellar door has been left open, as though the keeper expected to return.
A supply room lies beside the keeper's quarters.
Rope, hand tools, and spare hinges fill several wooden crates.
A maintenance record shows that the keeper repaired the service door shortly before disappearing.
The last line reads: 'The tower is ready. The sea will decide the rest.'
The upper doors open into the beacon chamber.
A great glass lens hangs above a circular platform.
The restored mechanism is connected to the lens by a series of brass arms.
A narrow stair leads to the chamber's highest platform.

success.message: You descend to the lantern platform. The beacon mechanism is ready whenever you return.

text: You step onto the focusing platform.
The two curved prisms now sit in their proper places.
The tide chart has aligned the mechanism with the sea's movement.
A final lever waits beneath the great lens.
You reach the highest platform and pull the lever.
The brass arms begin to turn. A warm light passes through the prisms and fills the chamber.
Far below, the beam sweeps across the dark water and reaches the open sea.
A distant ship answers with three bright lantern flashes.
Greyhaven's beacon is shining again. The harbor will have a safe way home.
Congratulations, {player.name}! You have restored The Last Light of Greyhaven.
THE END
